title: How do we get there?

goal: Use public transport in Georgia, buy tickets, stop a taxi, and use the -ით ending for every kind of transport at once.

dialogs.title: დიალოგი — A day trip to Mtskheta
dialogs.intro: Ani and Nino are planning a day trip to Mtskheta, an old town north of Tbilisi. Notice that every means of transport takes the same ending — the one you learned in unit 5 for "coffee with milk".

lines.speaker: ანი:
lines.id: How do we get to Mtskheta?

lines.speaker: ნინო:
lines.id: By marshrutka or by taxi. The marshrutka is cheaper.
lines.literal: marshrutka-by — or — taxi-by. marshrutka — more — cheap-is.

lines.speaker: ნინო:
lines.id: Three lari. A taxi would be about forty lari.
lines.literal: three — lari. taxi — forty — lari — will-be.

lines.speaker: ანი:
lines.id: Let's take the marshrutka. Where does it leave from?

lines.speaker: ნინო:
lines.id: From Didube station. We'll get there by metro.

lines.speaker: ანი:
lines.id: How long does the trip take?

lines.speaker: ნინო:
lines.id: Half an hour, if there's no traffic.
lines.literal: half — hour, if — traffic-jam — not — is.

lines.speaker: ნინო:
lines.id: We pay the driver directly. Have some small change ready!

lines.speaker: ნინო:
lines.id: At nine. A marshrutka leaves every twenty minutes.
lines.literal: nine — hour-at. marshrutka — every — twenty — minute-in — departs.

notes: **Every means of transport takes the -ით ending — one ending for all.** ავტობუს**ით** (by bus), მეტრო**თი** (by metro), ტაქს**ით** (by taxi), მატარებლ**ით** (by train), თვითმფრინავ**ით** (by plane), ფეხ**ით** (on foot). ⚠️ There's no preposition at all; don't look for a word for "by" or "on" — the ending already does that job.

**The მარშრუტკა is the backbone of Georgian transport.** A fourteen-seat minibus that runs a fixed route but stops anywhere if you signal. The word for stopping: **გამიჩერეთ!** (gamicheret — stop for me!), or more gently *აქ გავალ* (ak gaval — I'll get off here).

**Pay the driver, and have exact change ready.** On a marshrutka you pay when you get on or when you get off, depending on the route. ⚠️ A 50 or 100 lari note will be refused; *ხურდა გქონდეს* (have change ready) is serious advice.

**წავიდეთ, მივიდეთ, გავიდეთ — three "let's…" forms of motion verbs.** The ending **-ეთ**/-ოთ means "let's…". წავიდეთ (let's go), მივიდეთ (let's get there), ვიყიდოთ (let's buy). You don't need to form them yourself yet; just recognize what they mean.
**სჭირდება = is needed.** A close relative of მჭირდება (I need) from unit 7. *რამდენი ხანი სჭირდება?* — how long does it take? The standard way to ask how long any trip takes.
**საცობი = traffic jam.** An everyday word in Tbilisi, as in any big city. *საცობია* (there's traffic), *საცობში ვარ* (I'm stuck in traffic).
**ყოველ ოც წუთში = every twenty minutes.** A handy pattern: ყოველ საათში (every hour), ყოველ დღე (every day), ყოველ კვირას (every week).

grammars.title: Means of transport with the -ით ending
after: Notice **მეტრო → მეტროთი**: words ending in a vowel insert -თ before -ი. And **მატარებელი → მატარებლით**: the ე in the last syllable drops out. You'll get used to these two small exceptions with practice.

grammars.title: Must-know sentences on public transport

head: Sentence
Say it
Meaning
rows: Where do I have to change?

after: For taxis: apps (Bolt, Yandex) are widely used in Tbilisi and spare you the haggling. If you hail one on the street, ask the price **before** you get in: *რამდენი გამიწევს …-მდე?* (ramdeni gamits'evs …mde — how much to…?).

blocks.title: Three practical things about getting around Tbilisi
items: **The metro and buses are paid by card** (მეტრომანი / Metromoney) or a contactless bank card. One ride is about one lari, and transfers within ninety minutes are free.

**Intercity marshrutkas leave from bus stations**, not from ordinary stops: დიდუბე (west and north), ისანი (east), ორთაჭალა (south). There's no fixed timetable — a minibus leaves as soon as it's full.

**The train to Batumi** leaves from სადგურის მოედანი and is far more comfortable than a marshrutka for long trips. Buy tickets online or at the station; the phrase you need: *ბილეთი ბათუმამდე* (a ticket to Batumi).

blocks.text: Two words you'll see on every sign: **გასვლა** (gasvla — exit/departure) and **შესვლა** (shesvla — entrance). In metro stations, **გამოსასვლელი** means the exit. All three come from the same motion-verb root, and once you spot -სვლ- in the middle of a word, lots of signs start to make sense on their own.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.

items: How do we get to Mtskheta?
How long does the trip take?
I'm getting off at the next stop.
